page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6e.large is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor architecture (x86_64) operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 dedicated physical cores, providing 2 vCPUs, and is paired with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per core memory-to-CPU ratio. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage options. Network connectivity is established with a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place this instance in the lower tiers of compute and memory throughput. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance is rated as weak, scoring 1305.19, while the multi-core CPU performance drops into the poor category at 1737.28. Memory bandwidth tests show poor results, with read-only small block cached speeds at 96.8 GB/sec and uncached large block write speeds at 11.91 GB/sec. PassMark CPU and memory scores also reflect these limitations, with a database operations score of 708.59 and a static web serving throughput of 2.0 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.c6e.large is its constrained memory capacity of 4.0 GB and low multi-core processing efficiency, which limits its utility for memory-intensive or highly parallelized workloads. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance represents a low-resource entry point within the dedicated compute-optimized class, offering a predictable CPU allocation without the performance variability of shared-core models. It is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded tasks, basic web serving, simple utility scripts, or development and testing environments that do not require high memory or storage throughput.
